chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman sees blood for three or four days.' He said: 'She should leave the salat.' I said: 'Suppose she sees purity for three or four days.' He said: 'She should pray.' I said: 'Suppose she sees blood for three or four days.' He said: 'She should leave the salat.' I said: 'Suppose she sees purity for three or four days.' He said: 'She should pray.' I said: 'Suppose she sees blood for three or four days.' He said: 'She should leave the salat. She should keep doing so for what is between her and a month. When the blood stops from her (all is well), otherwise she is at the status of the woman with istihadha.'

key_terms.الطُّهْر: Purity/clean period — the days between menstrual blood episodes when no blood is present
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَة: Mustahadha — a woman experiencing istihadha, i.e., irregular or continuous bleeding that is not classified as haydh (menstruation); subject to specific jurisprudential rules
key_terms.انْقَطَعَ الدَّم: The blood ceased — the stopping of bleeding which signals return to normal purity
key_terms.تَدَعُ الصَّلَاة: She leaves/omits the salat — the ruling that a menstruating woman is exempt from obligatory prayers during her period

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman who alternates between blood and purity for three or four days according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a woman who experiences alternating blood and purity periods of three to four days each should follow the normal menstruation rules (leaving salat during blood and praying during purity) for up to one month. If the blood does not stop within a month, she transitions to the legal status of the mustahadha — a woman with irregular or inter-period bleeding — which carries different obligations. This hadith addresses a common but complex medical scenario and sets a clear one-month threshold before reclassification occurs.
